Assessment of commit c5a87a4 (worktree `/home/mark/acp/acp-java-conformance`) against roster acp-v1-2797d331-r1. Evidence is the SDK source plus tests; I ran the cited acp-core tests offline at this commit (`./mvnw -o -pl acp-core test`, 42 classes, 467 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors; surefire reports under acp-core/target/surefire-reports). Paths below are repository-relative; `AcpSchema.java` means acp-core/src/main/java/com/agentclientprotocol/sdk/spec/AcpSchema.java, and other acp-core files are under acp-core/src/main/java/com/agentclientprotocol/sdk/ (client/, agent/, spec/, capabilities/, client/transport/, agent/transport/) or acp-core/src/test/java/com/agentclientprotocol/sdk/ for tests.

ACP-V1-OVERVIEW-ABSOLUTE-PATHS: CANNOT_DETERMINE - The SDK composes no file paths itself and forwards application-supplied cwd/path strings verbatim (agent/DefaultPromptContext.java:150-157, AcpSchema.java:895, 1910); no absolute-path validation exists in main sources (grep for isAbsolute finds none), so conformance rests on the application.
ACP-V1-INIT-CLIENT-INITIALIZE-FIRST: PASS - initialize() sends LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION with the builder's capabilities (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:239-256) and every other call is refused until the agent has answered initialize (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:715-725; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:83-90).
ACP-V1-INIT-IMPLEMENTATION-INFO: PASS - clientInfo and agentInfo are modelled and sent when set (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:255-256 with client/AcpClient.java:304-308; agent/AcpAgent.java:1251-1255 and agent/DefaultInitialize.java:53), and the annotated-agent path derives a default agentInfo (acp-agent-support/src/main/java/com/agentclientprotocol/sdk/agent/support/AgentAdvertisement.java:265-279); the core builder/client omit them unless the application supplies its own identity.
ACP-V1-INIT-AGENT-RESPONSE: PASS - DefaultInitialize.respond answers with the negotiated protocolVersion and derived AgentCapabilities (agent/DefaultInitialize.java:44-54); protocolVersion is a required component (AcpSchema.java:729) and a result lacking it is rejected (spec/ResponseResults.java:664-668; spec/AcpClientSessionTest.java:533).
ACP-V1-INIT-VERSION-AGREEMENT: PASS - Both sides speak version 1 (AcpSchema.java:178); the client announces it (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:239-241) and the agent echoes a supported version or its latest (agent/DefaultInitialize.java:58-61; agent/BuilderDefaultsTest.java:41).
ACP-V1-INIT-REQUEST-LATEST-VERSION: PASS - initialize() announces LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:239-241, AcpSchema.java:178); spec/WireFormatTest.java:49-56 shows protocolVersion 1 on the wire.
ACP-V1-INIT-AGENT-SAME-VERSION: PASS - negotiate() returns the requested version when it is the supported one (agent/DefaultInitialize.java:58-61; AgentAdvertisement.java:304-307); agent/BuilderDefaultsTest.java:41.
ACP-V1-INIT-AGENT-LATEST-VERSION: PASS - For any other requested version negotiate() returns LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION (agent/DefaultInitialize.java:58-61; AgentAdvertisement.java:304-307).
ACP-V1-INIT-CLIENT-UNSUPPORTED-VERSION: FAIL - initialize() stores the agent's capabilities but never compares the answered protocolVersion with the one it supports, and neither closes nor warns; the Javadoc states "The client does not check the protocol version the agent answers with" (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:228-229, 258-266), leaving the SHOULD to the application without a stated reason.
ACP-V1-INIT-CAPABILITIES-OPTIONAL: PASS - Every capability component is @Nullable and null clientCapabilities/agentCapabilities are accepted (AcpSchema.java:693-696, 3347-3352, 3745-3751; capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:148-151, 188-191).
ACP-V1-INIT-SUPPORT-ALL-COMBINATIONS: PASS - NegotiatedCapabilities derives independent booleans per capability with no cross-constraint (capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:148-225), so any combination of a peer's flags is accepted.
ACP-V1-INIT-OMITTED-UNSUPPORTED: PASS - Omitted or null flags read as unsupported via Boolean.TRUE.equals and null-object checks (capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:157-175, 194-222); a non-object session capability reads as absent (AcpSchema.java:4090-4109; spec/SessionCapabilitiesWireTest.java:32-41).
ACP-V1-INIT-CLIENT-SPECIFY-CAPABILITIES: PASS - ClientCapabilities carries fs, terminal, session.configOptions.boolean, auth.terminal and elicitation with builder setters (AcpSchema.java:3347-3540); by default the client advertises what its handlers serve (client/AcpClient.java:703-726; client/ClientCapabilityDerivationTest.java:79-128).
ACP-V1-INIT-AGENT-SPECIFY-CAPABILITIES: PASS - The default initialize answer advertises loadSession, sessionCapabilities (list/close/resume/delete), auth.logout, mcp and prompt capabilities from the registered handlers (agent/DefaultInitialize.java:37-54; agent/BuilderDefaultsTest.java:47-60); unset ones are omitted, which the spec reads as unsupported.
OBSERVATION ACP-V1-INIT-AGENT-SPECIFY-CAPABILITIES: DefaultInitialize never advertises sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories (null at agent/DefaultInitialize.java:43); a builder agent needs its own initialize handler for it, while the annotated path can advertise it (AgentAdvertisement.java:313).
ACP-V1-INIT-PROMPT-BASELINE: PASS - PromptRequest.prompt is a List<ContentBlock> whose registered variants include text and resource_link (AcpSchema.java:1114-1116, 5304-5311, 5360, 5485) and the agent delivers them to the prompt handler unfiltered (agent/DefaultAcpAsyncAgent.java:98-106).
ACP-V1-INIT-PROMPT-RICHER-MAY: PASS - PromptCapabilities image/audio/embeddedContext (AcpSchema.java:4222-4243), builder shortcuts (AcpSchema.java:3878-3907) and the ImageContent/AudioContent/Resource types (AcpSchema.java:5405, 5442, 5528).
ACP-V1-INIT-SESSION-BASELINE: PASS - build() requires a prompt handler and installs a default session/new handler (agent/AcpAgent.java:1604-1619); session/cancel is always registered (agent/DefaultAcpAsyncAgent.java:90-91) and session/update is sent through sendSessionUpdate (agent/DefaultAcpAsyncAgent.java:190-192).
ACP-V1-INIT-SESSION-OPTIONAL-MAY: PASS - Optional session methods are advertised exactly when their handlers are registered (agent/DefaultInitialize.java:37-47; agent/BuilderDefaultsTest.java:47-60).
ACP-V1-AUTH-CLIENT-NO-LOGOUT-WITHOUT-CAPABILITY: PASS - logout() requires the negotiated auth.logout object before sending (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:315-320; capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:221-222, 597-599); spec/LogoutCapabilityTest.java:45-54 and client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:95-106.
ACP-V1-AUTH-CLIENT-NO-TERMINAL-METHOD-ID: FAIL - authenticate() sends any methodId after initialize without checking it against the advertised terminal methods; the Javadoc says "This method does not check the method's type" (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:291-301), so the MUST NOT is left to the application.
ACP-V1-AUTH-AGENT-TERMINAL-LOGIN-ARGS: PASS - The SDK models and transmits the terminal descriptor with args and env (AcpSchema.java:7462-7486; AgentAdvertisement.java:331-345; spec/TerminalAuthTest.java:51); the argument values are the agent program's.
ACP-V1-AUTH-CLIENT-AFTER-LOGOUT: PASS - An agent's -32000 error response fails the caller's request with an AcpError carrying that code rather than being hidden (spec/OutboundMessages.java:514-518; spec/AcpError.java:289-291; integration/ErrorCodePropagationTest.java:150).
ACP-V1-SETUP-INIT-BEFORE-SESSION: PASS - newSession() is gated by afterInitialize (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:338-344, 715-725; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:83-90).
ACP-V1-SETUP-NEW-SESSION-ID: PASS - sessionId is a required component (AcpSchema.java:948) that the client rejects when missing (spec/AcpClientSessionTest.java:541); the default session/new handler generates a fresh UUID per session (AcpSchema.java:986-988; agent/AcpAgent.java:1614-1618).
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLIENT-CHECK-LOADSESSION: PASS - loadSession() requires the negotiated loadSession flag (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:355-361; capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:194, 489-491; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:139-152).
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLIENT-NO-LOAD-WITHOUT-CAPABILITY: PASS - Without the flag loadSession() fails with AcpCapabilityException before anything is sent (capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:601-605; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:95-106).
ACP-V1-SETUP-LOAD-REQUEST-CONTENTS: PASS - LoadSessionRequest requires sessionId, cwd and mcpServers as non-null components (AcpSchema.java:1021-1024), enforced on receipt (spec/AcpTransport.java:99-113; spec/RequiredFields.java:591-600).
ACP-V1-SETUP-LOAD-REPLAY: PASS - The agent-aware loadSessionHandler receives the AcpAsyncAgent (agent/AsyncAgentAwareSetters.java:96-101) whose sendSessionUpdate is not gated to prompts (agent/DefaultAcpAsyncAgent.java:190-192), so the application can replay session/update notifications before completing the load response.
ACP-V1-SETUP-LOAD-RESPOND-AFTER-REPLAY: PASS - The session/load response is written only when the handler's Mono completes (spec/AcpAgentSession.java:267-270) and travels the same ordered outbound stream as notifications emitted before it (util/OutboundSinks.java:81-100; agent/transport/StdioAcpAgentTransport.java:480-489), so updates sequenced before the result precede it.
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLIENT-CHECK-RESUME: PASS - resumeSession() requires sessionCapabilities.resume (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:435-443; capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:200, 519-521; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:95-106).
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLIENT-NO-RESUME-WITHOUT-CAPABILITY: PASS - The same gating throws AcpCapabilityException and sends nothing (capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:601-605; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:95-106).
ACP-V1-SETUP-RESUME-REQUEST-CONTENTS: PASS - ResumeSessionRequest carries sessionId and cwd as required and mcpServers as a list (AcpSchema.java:1525-1549); the pinned schema's ResumeSessionRequest.required is ['sessionId','cwd'], so the SDK's optional mcpServers matches the wire contract while letting the client supply the servers.
OBSERVATION ACP-V1-SETUP-RESUME-REQUEST-CONTENTS: The prose lists MCP servers as required while protocol-conformance/spec/official/agent-client-protocol/schema/v1/schema.json requires only sessionId and cwd for ResumeSessionRequest; the SDK follows the schema (AcpSchema.java:1526).
ACP-V1-SETUP-RESUME-NO-REPLAY: PASS - The SDK's session/resume handling is a plain request handler that emits nothing of its own before the response (agent/AcpAgent.java:1416-1420; spec/AcpAgentSession.java:267-274); any replay would be the application's.
ACP-V1-SETUP-RESUME-RESPONSE-STATE-MAY: PASS - ResumeSessionResponse carries optional modes and configOptions (AcpSchema.java:1569-1588).
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLIENT-CHECK-CLOSE: PASS - closeSession() requires sessionCapabilities.close (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:401-407; capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:199, 509-511; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:95-106).
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLIENT-NO-CLOSE-WITHOUT-CAPABILITY: PASS - Same gating, AcpCapabilityException without a send (capabilities/NegotiatedCapabilities.java:601-605; client/ClientCallGatingTest.java:95-106).
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLOSE-REQUEST: PASS - CloseSessionRequest with required sessionId (AcpSchema.java:1413-1421) sent on session/close (client/AcpAsyncClient.java:401-407).
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLOSE-CANCELS-AND-FREES: PASS - On session/close the agent session cancels the active prompt as if session/cancel arrived, informs the cancel handler, waits for the turn to end, then runs the close handler (spec/AcpAgentSession.java:271-297); agent/SessionCloseCancelsPromptTest.java:52-92 asserts the order cancel, cancelled answer, close; freeing session resources is the close handler's.
ACP-V1-SETUP-CLOSE-MAY-ERROR: PASS - A close handler may throw AcpProtocolException, sent as the error response (spec/InboundMessages.java:127-130; integration/ErrorCodePropagationTest.java:150).

messages.content:
Assess the ACP Java SDK at c5a87a4638954612d3e1eb88eb75391a16a4e6fa against EVERY requirement in
the supplied stable ACP v1 roster, derived from 2797d33125c14e5bcfc815952930130c43e5bc4c
(roster revision acp-v1-2797d331-r1).
This is protocol conformance, including behavior and wire semantics.

Investigate the configured workspace. Read implementation code, tests,
schema and configuration; run relevant local tests as needed.
Interpret each clause at its original RFC2119 strength: MAY permits
omission; SHOULD permits a reasoned, documented exception. Apply only
the declared role, responsibility and capability conditions. Assess
SDK behavior separately from behavior an application must supply.

Answer all supplied IDs exactly once, in roster order, using the
generated response grammar:
<ID>: PASS|FAIL|CANNOT_DETERMINE - <reason citing supporting file:line>
NOT_APPLICABLE is allowed only for IDs with a declared applicability
condition that demonstrably does not hold; explain why it does not.

Insufficient evidence means CANNOT_DETERMINE, not PASS or a guessed FAIL.
Do not invent requirements, evidence, citations or test outcomes.
An existing passing test supports only the behavior it actually checks.
